newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Canada pork group to visit Seoul to boost exports.
newsitem.headline: Canada pork group to visit Seoul to boost exports.

text.p: A group made up of officials of the Canadian Pork Council and provincial hog producing organisations will visit South Korea between February 17-19, a commercial official at the Canadian embassy in Seoul said on Wednesday.
"A delegation, consisting of 13 members from the Canadian Pork Council and provincial hog producers, will visit South Korean pork importers from Monday till Wednesday," Kim Jong-hoon told Reuters.
The delegation will leave on Wednesday for Japan, now the world's largest pork-importing country, Kim said.

Spources said the delegation wants to become more familiar with the requirements and opportunities available in the South Korean pork market, which is one of Canada's top five pork importers, and to inform pork buyers there of the initiatives underway in Canada to produce lean and wholesome pork.

They said the mission is the first such national undertaking, and evolves directly from the export diversification strategy that has been initiated through the pork sector's trade development arm, Canada Pork International.
The trade sources said pork has become a leading value-added agri-food export for Canada, which is now exporting it to more than 50 different countries.
